changes.before: If each worker loops 250 times, what is the final count?
changes.after: Protect a shared counter so two workers do not lose each other's changes.

before: count++ reads, adds and writes; it is not one indivisible operation. A synchronized instance method locks that instance monitor for the entire method. Both workers must call increment on the same Counter to coordinate.

Each worker makes 1000 protected increments. Both joins complete before the read, making the finished count visible. The synchronized getter also uses the same monitor; it does not make unrelated locks equivalent.
Expected output or behavior: 2000. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why locking a separate newly created object on every call would not protect the shared counter. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: count++ reads the old value, adds one, and writes it back. Those steps can overlap between workers. A synchronized instance method locks its object's monitor, a built-in lock, for the whole call. Both workers use the same Counter, so only one can run its synchronized method at a time.

Each worker adds one a thousand times. main joins both workers before reading, so both have finished and their work is visible. The synchronized get method uses the same object's lock; different objects' locks would not coordinate these updates.
The program prints 2000. Each of the two workers contributes a thousand protected additions.
The quiz reduces the number of turns in the shared task. Both workers still finish before the total is read.

before.question: If each worker loops 250 times, what is the final count?
choices: 250 because a monitor discards one worker
An unpredictable value despite the shared monitor and joins.
before.explanation: The shared monitor protects every increment and both workers complete before the read.

after.question: Make each worker loop 250 times. What is the final count?
choices: 250, because the lock discards one worker's changes.
An unpredictable value, even with the shared lock and both joins.
after.explanation: Each worker contributes 250. The shared lock protects every addition, and both joins finish before the total of 500 is read.
